cues.en: (bright music)
cues.zh: （輕快音樂）

cues.en: Instructor: Welcome back, everyone.
cues.zh: 歡迎大家回來。

cues.en: We just discussed how to evaluate performance for classification problems.
cues.zh: 剛討論了分類問題的效能評估。

cues.en: Now let's understand how to evaluate performance for regression tasks.
cues.zh: 現在理解迴歸任務如何評估。

cues.en: So we're gonna take a moment to discuss how do we evaluate a model which is performing some sort of regression task.
cues.zh: 花點時間討論，模型執行迴歸任務時怎麼評估。

cues.en: And in general, a regression is a task when a model attempts to predict continuous values unlike those classification tasks where we're trying to predict categorical values.
cues.zh: 一般而言，迴歸是模型嘗試預測連續值的任務，不同於預測類別值的分類。

cues.en: So you may have heard of some evaluation metrics, such as accuracy, or recall, or precision, like we just discussed.
cues.zh: 你可能聽過剛才討論的準確率、召回率、精確率等指標。

cues.en: However, these sort of metrics aren't going to be useful for regression problems.
cues.zh: 但它們不適用迴歸問題。

cues.en: It doesn't really make sense to calculate the accuracy or recall of a regression task since you're actually classifying things.
cues.zh: 計算迴歸任務的準確率或召回率沒什麼意義，因為不是在分類。

cues.en: Instead, you're predicting a continuous value.
cues.zh: 而是在預測連續值。

cues.en: So we need new metrics designed for those continuous values.
cues.zh: 所以需要專門針對連續值的指標。

cues.en: For example, imagine we're attempting to predict the price of a house given its features.
cues.zh: 例如根據房屋特徵預測價格。

cues.en: That would be a regression task or attempting to predict the country a house is in given its features.
cues.zh: 這是迴歸任務；如果根據特徵預測房屋位在哪個國家，

cues.en: That would be a classification task.
cues.zh: 就是分類任務。

cues.en: And again, we're focused right now on how to evaluate that regression task where a label is continuous and it's not separate categories.
cues.zh: 現在專注評估標籤是連續值、而非獨立類別的迴歸任務。

cues.en: So we're gonna discuss the most common evaluation metrics for regression, which are mean absolute error, mean squared error, and then root mean squared error.
cues.zh: 要討論最常見的迴歸指標：平均絕對誤差、均方誤差、均方根誤差。

cues.en: So let's begin with the simplest, which is mean absolute error.
cues.zh: 先從最簡單的平均絕對誤差開始。

cues.en: And this one's the easiest to understand.
cues.zh: 這個最容易理解。

cues.en: Essentially all you're gonna do is you're gonna compare your predictions.
cues.zh: 基本上就是比較預測。

cues.en: And remember we're comparing a continuous value here since this is a regression task.
cues.zh: 記得是迴歸，所以比較連續值。

cues.en: We're gonna compare our predictions to the true y label.
cues.zh: 把預測與真實 y 標籤比較。

cues.en: For example, compare the actual prediction of the house price with the true house price.
cues.zh: 例如把預測房價與真實房價比較。

cues.en: And what we do is we just take the difference between the true price minus our predicted price.
cues.zh: 計算真實價格減去預測價格的差。

cues.en: That's y hat.
cues.zh: 預測值就是 ŷ。

cues.en: And we take the absolute value of that.
cues.zh: 再取絕對值。

cues.en: And the reason we take the absolute value is because technically our predictions could be over or under the true value.
cues.zh: 因為技術上，預測可能高於或低於真實值。

cues.en: And since we want to average this out across all our predictions, we take the absolute value.
cues.zh: 想對所有預測取平均，所以先取絕對值。

cues.en: Okay? So that's the mean absolute error.
cues.zh: 好，這就是平均絕對誤差。

cues.en: Essentially, you're just taking the differences between your prediction versus the true label.
cues.zh: 基本上取預測與真實標籤的差，

cues.en: You take the absolute value of that and then you average that out for all your predictions.
cues.zh: 取絕對值，再對所有預測取平均。

cues.en: Now the issue with mean absolute error is it won't punish large errors.
cues.zh: 平均絕對誤差的問題是，不會特別懲罰大誤差。

cues.en: So here we have what's known as Anscombe's quartet and we can see here that we have a wide variety of different scatters of data points here.
cues.zh: 這裡是 Anscombe 四重奏，可以看到不同的資料點散佈型態。

cues.en: However, the line of best fit for all of these is actually the same.
cues.zh: 但所有圖的最佳擬合直線其實相同。

cues.en: So we wanna make sure that we're aware of situations like this.
cues.zh: 所以要注意這類情況。

cues.en: For example, let's take a look at this specific situation where we have one point that's a huge outlier.
cues.zh: 例如這裡有一個非常大的離群點。

cues.en: So we want our error metrics to actually account for these.
cues.zh: 希望誤差指標能考量它。

cues.en: So what we can do is actually use mean squared error.
cues.zh: 可以使用均方誤差。

cues.en: And this is the mean of the squared errors.
cues.zh: 也就是平方誤差的平均。

cues.en: So what what we're doing here is we're gonna take the difference between the true value minus our predicted value, and we're gonna square it.
cues.zh: 取真實值減預測值，再平方。

cues.en: And as you can imagine, when we actually take that square, the larger errors are noted more than with mean absolute error, which makes mean squared error more popular
cues.zh: 可以想像，平方後，大誤差會比平均絕對誤差更突出，所以均方誤差比較熱門，

cues.en: because you're really gonna punish your model for those outlier situations that it's not fitting to.
cues.zh: 因為對沒有擬合好的離群情況，會更強烈懲罰模型。

cues.en: And we no longer need to take the absolute value because anything squared ends up being positive.
cues.zh: 而且不用再取絕對值，因為平方後是正的。

cues.en: However, there's another issue that we run into with mean squared error.
cues.zh: 不過均方誤差還有另一個問題。

cues.en: That squaring of the actual label minus our prediction actually also squares the units themselves.
cues.zh: 將實際標籤減預測再平方，也把單位平方了。

cues.en: So for example, if we're predicting the price of a house then our error metric of mean absolute error would be in dollars.
cues.zh: 例如預測房價，平均絕對誤差的單位是美元。

cues.en: But with mean squared error, we end up getting an error metric in units of dollars squared, which is difficult to interpret.
cues.zh: 但均方誤差的單位會是美元平方，很難解讀。

cues.en: So the way we fix this is with the root mean squared error, essentially at the end, you just take the square root of your mean squared error.
cues.zh: 解法是均方根誤差，最後把均方誤差開根號。

cues.en: So this is the most popular because it does both punish those larger error values and at the end of the day, it has the same metrics or same units as y.
cues.zh: 它最熱門，因為既懲罰較大的誤差，最後也和 y 有相同單位。

cues.en: Now the most common question again I get from students is, hey, is this value of root mean squared error I got good?
cues.zh: 學生最常問的依然是：「我得到這個均方根誤差，夠好嗎？」

cues.en: And as always, context is everything.
cues.zh: 一樣，脈絡最重要。

cues.en: Let's imagine you were performing some sort of machine learning model, and you got a root mean squared error of $10.
cues.zh: 假設做機器學習模型，得到 10 美元的均方根誤差。

cues.en: And you're asking me is this good enough root means squared error?
cues.zh: 你問這夠好嗎？

cues.en: Well, it really depends on the context of the situation.
cues.zh: 真正要看情境。

cues.en: A root mean squared error of $10 would be fantastic if you're predicting the price of a house since $10 is tiny compared to the average price of a house.
cues.zh: 預測房價時，10 美元的均方根誤差非常好，因為相較平均房價，10 美元很小。

cues.en: But if your machine learning model was supposed to predict the price of a candy bar based on its features and your root mean squared error was $10 that's actually really bad.
cues.zh: 但如果根據特徵預測巧克力棒價格，均方根誤差 10 美元就很差。

cues.en: So what you should do is you should compare your error metric for the regression task to the average value of the label.
cues.zh: 所以應把迴歸誤差指標與標籤的平均值比較。

cues.en: That is the mean value in your dataset to try to get an intuition of its overall performance.
cues.zh: 也就是資料集中的平均值，對整體效能建立直覺。

cues.en: And as always, domain knowledge also plays a really important role here.
cues.zh: 領域知識同樣很重要。

cues.en: So machine learning, again, it's not done in a vacuum, it's usually done with a collaborative process.
cues.zh: 機器學習不是在真空中進行，通常是協作過程。

cues.en: So if you're predicting the prices of a house and you wanted to get an idea if your root means squared error was good or not, it's probably then a good idea to start talking
cues.zh: 如果預測房價，想知道均方根誤差好不好，可能應找

cues.en: to someone with experience like a real estate agent.
cues.zh: 有經驗的人，例如房仲，聊一聊。

cues.en: Okay, so now we understand the different metrics we can use for evaluating the performance of a regression task.
cues.zh: 好，現在理解能用哪些不同指標評估迴歸任務。

cues.en: Thanks, and I'll see you at the next lecture.
cues.zh: 謝謝，下一堂見。
